expectations.text: The response does not deliver a finished accessibility page immediately; it asks clarifying interview questions before committing to provisions.
expectations.evidence: Delivers a full copy-ready page: '## 2. Page draft (copy-ready)'. Interview questions come only as 'Assumptions to confirm' after the draft.

expectations.text: It asks whether a legal entity exists that can sign vendor contracts, carry insurance, and disburse money before entertaining childcare, equipment rental, or grants.
expectations.evidence: 'Q4, legal entity: I assumed you have none...' and closing 'answer Q1, Q4 and Q5 above'; childcare/grants are excluded on that basis.

expectations.text: It asks what access needs are already known or documented (previous edition requests, community reports, a declared speaker need) so provisioning happens against evidence before a template.
expectations.evidence: Q3 appears only as an assumption: 'I assumed... you have no documented access needs'. It is not put to the user as a question.

expectations.text: It asks whether anyone is available to staff a request channel from now through the event, and treats a no as deleting the request-channel options.
expectations.evidence: 'Q9... If not, delete the request channel and design everything to work walk-up.'

expectations.text: It warns that signing the venue contract before writing accessibility criteria forecloses most physical provisions, because those provisions are properties of the building.
expectations.evidence: 'almost every physical provision is a property of the building.' Once you sign, the menu is chosen for you.

expectations.text: It recommends writing an accessibility criteria sheet before Friday and checking the candidate venue against it, rather than treating the signed venue as a given.
expectations.evidence: 'Before Friday: venue criteria sheet'; 'Send this to the venue today and get answers in writing.'

expectations.text: It rejects copying the foundation's full templated page, identifying that page as the top of the published range that most events do not reach, never a floor or baseline.
expectations.evidence: 'I didn't copy the foundation's page. The skill calls the full page "the top of a range most published events do not reach."'

expectations.text: It states that at a community budget every provision competes with catering for the same money, and uses that funding pole to bound the depth of the recommended set.
expectations.evidence: 'Q1... every provision competes with catering'; 'one-pot-with-catering budget'; childcare, grants and rental are dropped.

expectations.text: It refuses to publish a page describing provisions not yet secured, naming the consequence that an attendee who travels on the promise finds it broken.
expectations.evidence: 'Delete any section whose provision you can't secure. Do not leave a promise standing.' 'Someone would travel on those promises and find out in the room.'

expectations.text: It recommends the published page plus request channel as the default depth rung, characterized as roughly an afternoon of work plus a staffed inbox.
expectations.evidence: The table says 'Published page and request channel, with a named inbox' but gives no effort characterization such as an afternoon of work.

expectations.text: It states that the funded-access set (childcare, equipment rental, grants) is dropped entirely, not merely deprioritized, if no legal entity can hold a contract.
expectations.evidence: 'No childcare, grants or equipment rental... Childcare needs a legal entity, insurance and vetting'; 'we do not offer these this year.'

expectations.text: It presents its ranking as a default to re-rank against the user's answers, not as a fixed rule.
expectations.evidence: 'Each changes the page if wrong'; 'If a sponsor or foundation later funds a line, re-rank captioning and childcare upward.'

expectations.text: The proposed provision set is presented item by item with an owner and effort cost per provision, each labelled as sourced practice or a self-set decision.
